about: Answer key, operator-only. The sweeps were made on 2026-11-11 through POST /api/sweep: 24 values of weightUdp (0.05 to 0.95, every 0.01 from 0.26 to 0.36) x 5 queue lengths (4, 8, 20, 100, 1000) x 6 TCP variants = 720 simulations per scheduling policy, duration 10, seed 1. The notes were drafted from the sweep tables and are the operator's to edit.

share.notes: Goal: largest tcp_goodput_bps while udp_loss_frac <= 0.01. With TcpCubic and queues of 100 packets, UDP stops losing packets from weightUdp 0.31 upward, and from there TCP goodput is the same at every weight (668.6 Mbps at 0.31, 0.5 and 0.9): TCP takes whatever UDP does not use. The best row of the grid is 670.8 Mbps at weightUdp 0.28, queuePkts 4, TcpNewReno, where UDP loses 0.7% (inside the condition); it is the only row within 0.1% of the best. Best per TCP variant: NewReno 670.8, LinuxReno 669.6, Bic 668.8, Cubic 668.6, Vegas 519.6, Bbr 411.4 Mbps. Queues of 1000 packets are worse (660.8). 535 of the 720 rows meet the condition.

cap.notes: Same goal. UDP stops losing packets from weightUdp 0.31 upward, as under share, but here TCP goodput falls as the weight rises (666.1 Mbps at 0.31, 482.7 at 0.5, 96.5 at 0.9): each flow is held to its part. The best row is 666.1 Mbps at weightUdp 0.31; twelve rows are within 0.1% of it, all at 0.31, with Cubic, LinuxReno, Bic or NewReno and queues of 4 to 100 packets. Vegas reaches 519.6 and Bbr 411.4 Mbps. 420 of the 720 rows meet the condition.

checklist: Finds that the setting only matters under contention / when the UDP flow uses less than its part
Finds the effect of a short queue with a hard-backing-off TCP variant
Does not spend simulations on differences smaller than run-to-run variation
